analysis.investment_thesis: Prime Focus fails the Magic Formula on both axes: Earnings Yield of ~2.5% (EBIT ₹787 Cr / EV ~₹31,441 Cr) is far below my 12% threshold, and ROCE of 7.95% is less than half my 20% minimum — you're paying a steep price for a mediocre-returning, debt-laden business. With net losses in 7 of 10 years and free cash flow negative three of the last four years, there is no "magic" here.
key_strengths: High gross margin (93.97%) reflects asset-light services model typical of VFX/post-production
Revenue CAGR of 11.2% over 9 years shows resilient top-line demand from Hollywood/OTT clients
Promoter holding of 60.76% signals conviction, and equity has recently recovered (₹1,739 Cr in 2025 vs near-zero in 2023)
key_risks: Chronic net losses — negative in 7 of 10 years; FY2025 net loss of ₹458 Cr despite ₹787 Cr EBIT means finance costs (₹538 Cr) are consuming nearly all operating profit
Debt spiral: borrowings grew from ₹3,371 Cr (2020) to ₹5,255 Cr (2025) at 8.3% CAGR, D/E at 2.46x, leaving almost no equity cushion
Free cash flow negative ₹337 Cr in FY2024 and ₹68 Cr in FY2025 — capex of ₹366 Cr in 2025 is eating OCF, so the business cannot self-fund growth
red_flags: Earnings Yield of ~2.5% (EBIT ₹787 Cr / EV ₹31,441 Cr) — Magic Formula requires >12%; this is 5x too expensive
ROCE of 7.95% is below cost of debt, meaning borrowings are destroying value, not creating it
EV/EBITDA of 46x on a business with deeply negative ROE (-16.7%) and no sustained earnings — price embeds heroic assumptions
Operating CF turned negative in FY2024 (-₹32 Cr), a warning sign that the core business struggled to generate cash despite ₹975 Cr EBITDA just a year prior in FY2023 — volatility is extreme
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Prime Focus yields two failing grades simultaneously. Earnings Yield = EBIT ₹787 Cr / EV (Market Cap ₹26,776 Cr + Debt ₹4,879 Cr − Cash ₹214 Cr = ₹31,441 Cr) = 2.5% — you need at least 12% to rank in the top decile, so this is priced like a premium growth compounder but delivers a mediocre-quality business. ROCE of 7.95% (and ROE of -16.7%) confirms the capital deployed is not earning adequate returns; this falls far below my 20% hurdle and 25% "excellent" threshold.

The structural problem is the debt load. Finance costs of ₹538 Cr in FY2025 consume 68% of EBIT, leaving nothing for equity holders — hence the ₹458 Cr net loss. Borrowings have grown every single year since 2020, and free cash flow has been negative three of the last four years. The FY2023 EBITDA spike to ₹1,232 Cr followed by a collapse to ₹383 Cr in FY2024 shows high earnings volatility, the opposite of the stable, high-ROIC businesses I seek. At P/E 102x (or even forward 49x) on a company that persistently loses money at the net level, the market is pricing in a dramatic turnaround that the capital structure makes very difficult to achieve.
